climate_pressure: Rising temperature, increasing evapotranspiration, recurrent agricultural drought.
documented_impact: Severe 2025 cereal losses and delayed 2026 planting.
fcv_mediator: Agricultural livelihood dependence, input prices, market access, household purchasing power and existing conflict-related vulnerability.
possible_consequence: Could increase food insecurity, harmful coping and livelihood-related mobility or humanitarian dependence; evidence here does not demonstrate increased violence.
geographies: with particular relevance to rainfed zones
uncertainty: The relative contribution of climate versus economic/security variables is not quantified.
compact_statement: Warming and drought can worsen agricultural and food stress through livelihoods and markets, but current evidence does not show that this automatically causes violence. (ODI: Think change1)

climate_pressure: Drought, heat-driven evapotranspiration and structural water stress.
documented_impact: Irrigation and WASH systems have degraded; greater reliance on groundwater has developed.
fcv_mediator: Conflict damage, weak maintenance, energy shortages and reduced institutional/service capacity.
possible_consequence: Climate shocks may produce larger livelihood and service impacts than they would with functional infrastructure.
geographies: with large variation by governorate and system
alternative_explanations: allocation decisions and upstream water management
uncertainty: Asset damage does not translate uniformly into functional service loss.
compact_statement: Conflict-damaged water and irrigation systems increase sensitivity to drought and heat, while coping through additional groundwater pumping may itself create new risk. (World Bank4)

climate_pressure: Severe multiyear drought in the late 2000s, against a warming/drying background.
documented_impact: Agricultural stress occurred, but the scale of “agricultural collapse” is disputed.
fcv_mediator: Agricultural policy, groundwater governance, economic liberalization, rural livelihoods, migration and urban socioeconomic stress.
possible_consequence: One literature strand argues these pressures contributed to unrest; other peer-reviewed studies find the migration and conflict links inadequately evidenced.
geographies: must not be generalized mechanically to all Syria
alternative_explanations: local political mobilization and other conflict drivers
uncertainty: High; major elements of the causal chain are contested.
resilience_factors: More sustainable water/agricultural policy and responsive social protection could reduce vulnerability
but counterfactual conflict effects are unknown
compact_statement: Pre-war drought may have interacted with agrarian and governance vulnerabilities, but the claim that it materially caused the Syrian war is not established. (Columbia OCP5)

climate_pressure: Rising heat, drought and water stress.
documented_impact: Millions of returns are occurring while substantial internal displacement and WASH deficits persist.
fcv_mediator: War-damaged housing and services, unresolved displacement, poverty and limited local absorption capacity.
possible_consequence: Returnees and host communities may face heightened climate/service exposure and, conditionally, secondary displacement or local service pressures.
uncertainty: No national study located that isolates climate's contribution to post-2024 return sustainability.
resilience_factors: protection and locally informed recovery planning
compact_statement: Large-scale returns into damaged service systems may raise exposure to climate and water stress, but evidence for resulting displacement or tension is not yet causal. (UNHCR Data Portal3)

documented_impact: A dedicated water-resilience programme is under implementation.
fcv_mediator: Security conditions caused temporary work suspension alongside other implementation delays.
possible_consequence: Delayed completion may prolong exposure to water scarcity; the magnitude of that effect has not been measured.
alternative_explanations: contract commencement and winter working conditions also caused delay
uncertainty: No evaluated estimate of foregone adaptation benefit.
resilience_factors: Flexible implementation schedules and conflict-sensitive programme management
compact_statement: Security conditions directly delayed a water-scarcity adaptation project, a traceable example of FCV constraining adaptation delivery. (Adaptation Fund16)

climate_pressure: Heat, drought and constrained water availability.
documented_impact: Aleppo programme locations adopted drip irrigation and other climate-smart practices; village committees incorporated adaptation into local plans.
fcv_mediator: Local-government capacity, participation, trust, equity and social cohesion.
possible_consequence: Participatory and climate-sensitive recovery may improve acceptance and resilience and could reduce tension risk; the latter has not been independently demonstrated.
institutions: FAO and UN Joint Programme agencies
alternative_explanations: economic improvement and improved security may independently increase acceptance
uncertainty: Programme self-report; no counterfactual or independent conflict outcome measurement.
compact_statement: Local adaptation and participatory institutions are plausible resilience assets, but peace-supporting effects remain programme-level claims rather than evaluated outcomes. (MPTF Gateway14)

documented_impact: Very low cereal production and unusually high wheat-import requirements.
fcv_mediator: Input costs, foreign-exchange availability, currency conditions, localized unrest and market access.
possible_consequence: Combined production and market shocks can worsen household food access and humanitarian need.
geographies: with stronger impacts in agricultural and conflict-affected areas
uncertainty: Attribution shares among climate and economic factors are not quantified.
compact_statement: Drought-driven production losses interact with market and economic constraints to deepen food-security risk without implying a climate-to-violence pathway. (FAOHome2)

climate_pressure: Drought, heat and increasing water stress.
documented_impact: Large WASH needs, low system functionality and untreated sewage.
fcv_mediator: Infrastructure damage, energy shortages, weak maintenance, displacement and humanitarian-access constraints.
possible_consequence: Water-quality and availability problems can increase health and humanitarian-service burdens, particularly among displaced and poor populations.
alternative_explanations: waste-management failure and energy shortages can create WASH risks independently of climate
uncertainty: Disease outcomes were not separately attributed to climate in the sources used.
resilience_factors: water-quality management and emergency service continuity
compact_statement: Climate water stress acts on already damaged WASH systems, while conflict-related infrastructure and access conditions reduce the capacity to absorb that stress. (UNICEF9)
